title: Editing Blueprint (EBP) v1
description: A renderer-agnostic, timecoded specification of editing craft extracted from a reference video. Contains NO pixel or audio data from the reference. See docs/06-blueprint-spec.md.

Confidence.description: 0 = pure guess, 1 = directly measured. Consumers MUST degrade behaviour below 0.6.

source_fingerprint.description: Perceptual hash of the reference. NOT a copy of it.

semantic_backend.description: Which semantic backend produced the shot labels (vlm, clip, heuristic, none). A blueprint built with heuristics and one built with a VLM are not comparable, and the analysis cache must not serve one where the other was expected.

safe_area_inset_pct.description: Platform UI chrome to keep clear of. TikTok right rail, IG caption bar, etc.

AudioTrack.description: The reference's RHYTHMIC SKELETON. Never audio data. The renderer binds this to a licensed track via music_binding.

bpm_curve.description: Tempo changes as [time_ms, bpm] pairs. Empty means constant tempo.

target_cut_density.description: Cuts per second the renderer should aim for in this section when adapting to a different-length track.

bound_to_cut.description: Index into cuts[] this SFX punctuates.

MusicBinding.description: How the rhythmic skeleton is realised with real audio at render time. There is deliberately NO strategy that muxes the reference's master recording into the export. 'platform_attach' is how a user gets the original track: silent master, sound attached in-app under the platform's licence.

time_map.description: Warp from blueprint time to bound-track time as [bp_ms, track_ms] anchor pairs. Handles tempo mismatch without pitch-shifting.

summary.description: Human-readable. Rendered on the style card.

beat_lock_ratio.description: Fraction of cuts within tolerance of a beat or subdivision.

offset_mean_ms.description: Mean signed cut offset from beat. Typically negative for expert edits.

acceleration.description: -1 decelerating, 0 steady, +1 accelerating across the piece.

effect_budget.description: Max instances per effect type per section. Reproducing restraint matters as much as reproducing vocabulary.

embedding.description: Style vector for similarity search. Length is model-dependent.

Slot.description: A hole in the timeline that a user clip segment must fill. The matcher's unit of work.

importance.description: 1.0 = load-bearing (the drop shot). Low-importance slots are dropped first under insufficiency.

motion_direction_deg.description: Required for whip-pan and directional transitions to work.

semantic_hint.description: Natural-language description of the reference shot, for VLM re-ranking.

droppable.description: May be removed under insufficient footage.

Assignment.description: Resolved at match time. Absent in a fresh blueprint; present in a project-bound one.

reason.description: Surfaced in the swap UI. Explaining the choice is what makes corrections informative.

locked.description: User pinned this. The matcher must not move it.

offset_ms.description: Signed offset from the anchor beat. Negative = early. Preserving this is a large part of why output feels professionally cut.

hide_in_motion.description: Renderer may nudge +/-3 frames to a motion-energy peak.

secondary.description: Layered transitions. A whip pan is usually also motion_blur.

align.description: Where the cut sits within the transition interval.

fallback.description: Used when footage cannot support the primary (e.g. no lateral motion for a whip pan).

MotionTrack.description: Synthetic camera motion applied to a still or moving clip: push-in, drift, rotate.

relative_to_subject.description: Anchor the motion on the tracked subject centroid rather than frame centre.

interpolation.description: optical_flow is expensive; reserved for Pro export.

Grade.description: Parametric, not a recovered LUT. See docs/08 section 5 for why exact LUT recovery is not possible from a delivered video.

lut_ref.description: Optional ID of a LICENSED LUT from our library that best approximates the measured look. Never a LUT extracted from the reference.

match_target.description: Measured colour statistics of the reference. The renderer optimises the user's footage toward these rather than blindly applying params.

active_word_style.description: For karaoke mode: how the currently-spoken word differs.

lead_ms.description: Offset from the ASR word timestamp.

TextStyle.description: font_family is a CLASSIFIED family mapped to a licensed font, not an identified typeface. Exact font identification from compressed video is unreliable.

size_pct.description: Cap height as a percentage of frame height.

TextObject.description: Titles, lower-thirds and graphics that are NOT speech captions.

content.description: Null means the user must supply. We never copy the reference's words.

ReframeTrack.description: How source footage is cropped/panned into the canvas. Subject-aware, not centre-crop.

subject_query.description: Concept prompt handed to the segmentation model, e.g. 'the motorcycle'.

smoothing.description: Higher = lazier virtual camera. Prevents jitter from per-frame mask noise.

Constraints.description: Invariants the renderer must not violate. These are what stop degradation from producing garbage.

min_shot_ms.description: Below ~180ms a shot is not perceived as a shot.

require_licensed_audio.description: Not configurable. The renderer refuses to run without a resolved licence.

Degradation.description: Populated by the renderer when the blueprint could not be fully realised. Surfaced in the UI and stamped into export metadata.

PlatformAttachCard.description: Instructions for re-attaching the original sound INSIDE the platform, under the platform's own licence. Contains no audio, no download URL and no track file -- only the identifiers a human reads off the screen and the arithmetic to line the sound up with our cuts.

sound_name.description: Platform-native sound name as displayed. We surface what the reference credits; we do not fetch or host the audio.

trim_start_ms.description: Offset into the platform track where our first frame sits. The number the creator types into the sound-trim control.

first_downbeat_ms.description: Where the first downbeat lands in OUR output, so alignment can be verified visually.
